title: Quinoa vs. Bulgur: Nutrition Compared

seo.title: Quinoa vs. Bulgur: Nutrition Compared
seo.meta_description: Cooked bulgur usually has more fiber and fewer calories; quinoa has slightly more protein and is naturally gluten-free. Compare per 100 g cooked.
seo.search_intent: Compare quinoa and bulgur for protein, fiber, calories, gluten, and minerals.

excerpt: Per 100 g cooked, quinoa provides about 120 calories, 4.4 g protein, and 2.8 g fiber; bulgur about 83 calories, 3.1 g protein, and 4.5 g fiber. Bulgur is whole wheat and contains gluten, while quinoa is naturally gluten-free.
content_html:
Quinoa and bulgur are both marketed as healthy alternatives to rice, but they do not win the same categories. Bulgur provides substantially more fiber and fewer calories per 100 g cooked, while quinoa has a modest protein edge and is naturally gluten-free. Putting the numbers side by side makes the choice much more concrete.

Cooked nutrition per 100 g

QuinoaBulgur
Calories~120~83
Protein~4.4 g~3.1 g
Fiber~2.8 g~4.5 g

Quinoa provides about 1.3 g more protein, but bulgur adds roughly 1.7 g more fiber and about 37 fewer calories per 100 g cooked. Calling either one simply “more nutritious” hides the useful parts of the comparison.

At a 180 g cooked serving, bulgur would provide about 8.1 g fiber versus roughly 5 g from quinoa. For someone actively trying to raise fiber intake, that gap can matter more than quinoa's small protein advantage.

Why bulgur retains so much fiber

Bulgur is made from whole wheat that is parboiled, dried, and cracked. It keeps the whole-grain components, so it retains more fiber than many refined wheat products.

It also absorbs a lot of water during cooking, which helps explain its low calorie density per 100 g. Cooking is not making calories disappear; the energy is spread through a more hydrated food.

Gluten can decide the choice immediately

Bulgur contains gluten because it is wheat. Quinoa is a pseudocereal and is naturally gluten-free. For celiac disease or any diet that requires strict gluten avoidance, that distinction is much more important than the small protein difference.

They do not behave exactly the same in the kitchen

Fine bulgur can hydrate quickly and has a pleasantly chewy texture that works well in tabbouleh, salads, and side dishes. Quinoa stays more separate, with smaller grains and a relatively neutral flavor.

Either can form a useful base for vegetables, legumes, fish, or meat. The real choice is about texture and nutritional priorities rather than one food being universally better.

Which one should you choose?

For more fiber with relatively few calories, bulgur is especially strong if gluten is not an issue. For a gluten-free base with slightly more protein, quinoa has the advantage. There is no overall winner because they optimize different things.

faq.question: Which has more fiber?
faq.answer: Cooked bulgur usually has more: around 4.5 g/100 g versus roughly 2.8 g/100 g for quinoa.

faq.question: Which has more protein?
faq.answer: Quinoa usually has a modest edge: about 4.4 g/100 g versus 3.1 g/100 g.

faq.question: Does bulgur contain gluten?
faq.answer: Yes. Bulgur is made from wheat.
